intended_object: The canonical homeomorphism over X between the universal cover X̃ (at basepoint x₀) and its orbit quotient X̃/{1} by the trivial subgroup of π₁(X, x₀). Its underlying map is the quotient map. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (the subgroup-to-cover direction of the classification of covering spaces).
explanation:
The definition matches its docstring. The underlying function is the quotient map `subgroupQuotientMap x₀ ⊥`. It is bijective because the orbit relation of the trivial subgroup is equality; the proof uses `orbitRelQuotientBotEquiv`. Continuity and openness come from the fact that the quotient map is a covering map. So the result really is the canonical identification over X that the docstring describes.

The typeclass hypotheses `LocallyPathConnectedSpace X` and `SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace X` are not strictly needed: a bijective quotient map is always a homeomorphism. But they are exactly the textbook conditions under which the universal cover is constructed and the classification is stated. The generality is therefore the standard one for this object, not an artificial narrowing.

Mathlib has no general universal-cover construction, so it has no counterpart to this map.
